newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares trim early losses to settle lower.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares trim early losses to settle lower.

text.p: Greek equities traded in negative territory but trimmed early losses to settle lower with the correction holding around 960 points on the benchmark index. Brokers said profit taking continued in healthy trading volume of 10 billion drachmas.

"We had more profit taking today especially from certain mutual and closed-end investment funds with the market bouncing off its session low of 959 points on the benchmark index. Trading volumes remain strong with banks stocks likely to move higher," said broker Gregory Vlahos at Pegasos Securities.
"The market could rebound on Thursday and Friday with players positioning ahead of the election outcome, discounting the victory of either of the two major parties," he said.
Vlahos said his favourite picks included engineering firm Metka and OTE telecoms OTEr.AT, both expected to deliver strong returns later in the year.
Greece will hold early elections September 22.

The Athens general share index closed 0.33 percent, or 3.17 points lower at 963.47 from Tuesday's 966.64 close after opening at 965.03 points. Turnover fell to 10.1 billion drachmas from 12.4 billion on Tuesday on volume of 5.1 million shares.
Losers led gainers 125 to 75 with 41 issues unchanged on 241 traded. Banks slipped 0.44 percent, industrials eased 0.07 percent and construction lost 0.44 percent. Small-caps firmed by 0.08 percent.
On Friday, market watchers sensed the beginning of a bull trend saying further gains could unfold with the market discounting a strong government after the elections.

The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 555-573 at the close. Shares of OTE telecom OTEr.AT, the underlying, ended down 20 drachmas at 4,050 after moderate trade.

The recently launched Merrill Lynch stock index call warrant based on a basket of 23 shares was quoted lower at 212.20-223.40 drachmas. It expires on January 9 1998 with a strike price of 1000. It was in the money at 1051.8.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted lower at 4,496-4,772 drachmas at the close.
